title: Implement a bounded recent-use cache
prompt: Implement an LRU cache for string keys and string values with a positive capacity. get(key) returns the value, or null when absent, and marks a hit as most recently used. put(key, value) inserts or replaces a value and marks it most recently used. If a new key exceeds capacity, evict the least recently used key. Aim for average O(1) get and put. Explain the invariants and show what happens for capacity 2: put('a','1'), put('b','2'), get('a'), put('c','3'), get('b').
followUps: Does replacing an existing key change the number of entries?
How do you keep lookup and recency structures consistent?
What happens at capacity one and on a missing get?

twist.prompt: Entries now have a time-to-live. Explain how expiration interacts with recency and which complexity guarantees you can retain.

hints: A lookup map alone does not encode recency changes efficiently.
Think of a structure that removes and moves a known entry in constant time.
Maintain explicit invariants between the lookup map and the recency order.
